SMTO-UI-0056 — SMTO's sign-in isn't set up on this server

GUID: 15702bbd-eb04-55b0-b3ca-8dac4f129a6c
Slug: portal-setup-required
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • SMTO can't check anyone's username and password because its sign-in setup on the server is missing or can't be read. Nobody can sign in until it's fixed. This check doesn't change your conversations or tasks.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell the person who installed or manages SMTO that the page says sign-in isn't set up. Sign-in setup can only be finished on the server computer, not from your browser.
  2. If you manage SMTO: on the server computer, run aor auth setup, or run the SMTO Server installer again, using the same SMTO data folder as before. This creates the sign-in accounts that SMTO checks before letting anyone in.
  3. If sign-in was set up before and only the administrator's username or password needs replacing, run aor auth reset on the server computer instead. Reset replaces the sign-in details without setting up the server from scratch.
  4. When setup finishes, reload the sign-in page in your browser. SMTO checks its sign-in setup again each time the page loads.

What success looks like

  • The page shows Sign in to your workspace and accepts your username and password.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the server log names the exact sign-in storage problem. Don't delete or reset the SMTO data folder to get past this, because it holds everyone's conversations. Never include passwords or browser cookies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The portal auth middleware returned portal_setup_required (503) because the account store raised AuthUnavailable: the sign-in storage in the auth directory is missing, unreadable, behind a link, full, or failed its owner-migration check.

What this means

  • The server has no usable sign-in setup for this request. This reports access to the current request, not the outcome of previous operations.

Why this can happen

  • The server has no usable sign-in setup for this request.

How to diagnose it

  • The server accepts sign-in with the configured account.

How to fix it

  • On the Server host, run aor auth setup (or rerun the Server installer) for the same state directory, then reload the sign-in page; run aor auth reset only if the credentials must be replaced. If setup already ran, read the AuthUnavailable message in the Server log (unreadable or linked auth path, storage full, owner migration backup mismatch) and fix that auth directory's permissions or contents.
  • The server owner must complete local authentication setup using the application’s aor auth setup command and its existing state directory. Then reopen sign-in.

Retry and execution caution

  • The server accepts sign-in with the configured account.

How to verify the fix

  • The server accepts sign-in with the configured account.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
